title: FIG. 4. CARLISLE, COURSE OF THE WALL AND OF THE YALLUM.
name: Carlisle, plan of the course of the Wall and of the Vallum between Stanwix and the Castle, with the 1857-58 great sewer, Maclauchlan (1858)
desc: Maclauchlan, Memoir, Written During a Survey of the Roman Wall (1858), Fig. 4: the binder's directions (djvu leaf 119) say 'The Plans, Fig. 4, 6, Carlisle and the Camp on Skew Hill at page 76.'; the running head on p.77 is 'CARLISLE, COURSE OF THE WALL AND OF THE YALLUM.' (See Plans, Fig. 4.). Plan of Carlisle: the course of the Wall and the Vallum between Stanwix and the Castle, with the 1857-58 great sewer and its drain; 'H M^L delin', Sandridge & Co. Litho London. The only site plan still legible in this copy (n0078 and n0111 are blank here - docs/lead_roman.md). Internet Archive memoirwrittendu00maclgoog, leaf n0093 of the 171-leaf 1858 original.

title: Innerpeffery camp. and Ardoch camp.
name: The legionary camps of Ardoch and Innerpeffery, two plans, Horsley (1732), P.44
desc: Horsley, Britannia Romana (1732), P.44 (leaf n0114): the two legionary camps of the Mons Graupius campaign per the book's text pp.43-44 ('the legions might poflibly have been at Ardoch, or Innerpeffery, before they marched to the battle'): Ardoch camp (the lower plan, concentric with a Praetorium box, the Knoch river on its west and the Ruchel to its north) and the Innerpeffery camp (the upper plan, a single circuit with a military way and 'a bank by which the river has formerly run'; each plan with its 200-yard scale). The Ardoch row is the Braco camp (Q4788225, Gask Ridge - DECISIONS 808 148); the Innerpeffery camp is recorded here on this row (the 808 box: no row of its own). Internet Archive britanniaromanao00hors, leaf n0114 of the 936-leaf Google scan (British Museum volume).

title: The five fecondary ftations per lineam valli
name: The five secondary stations per lineam valli, five fort plans, Horsley (1732), P.113
desc: Horsley, Britannia Romana (1732), P.113 (leaf n0185): five fort plans - I GLANNIBANTA (Lanchester), II ALIONE (Whitley castle), III BREMETEN RACUM (Old Penrith), IV OLENACUM (Old Carlisle), V VIROSIDUM (near Elenborough), with Praetorium boxes on I and III, Watling Street, a compass and 'A feale of 100 paces'. I-IV have catalog rows (longovicium-q6674222, whitley-castle-q7996561, voreda-roman-fort-q17642742, luguvallium-q71551754); the row ties to V VIROSIDUM, the only one of the five without a catalog row, as the plate's new no-QID 'roman fort' row - all five plans are equal, so no other ranking (DECISIONS 808 147 item 4). Internet Archive britanniaromanao00hors, leaf n0185 of the 936-leaf Google scan (British Museum volume).

desc: Horsley, Britannia Romana (1732), P.158 N.10 (leaf n0254): a two-landscape-page fold-out of the wall from Congavata to Tunnocelum: the west part shows CONGAVATA 'now Stanwicks' at the Eden mouth (Grinfdale, Stenton, Etterby), the east part shows TVNNOCEIVM 'now Boulneis' by Braken ridge on the Solway shore north of the Esk estuary (ITVNNAE AESTVARIVM; the Esk mouth with Ronciff at the SW of the map), with Gabrosentum, Drumbrugh, Axelodunum, Brugh, the Solway Frith, and Hadrian's and Severus's vallums.
